title: In-Person Recording Is Live: The Best Conversation of the Quarter Shouldn't Live in Someone's Memory
summary: In-Person Recording is live in Hyperbound Perform. Record across-the-table sales conversations in your browser and score them alongside every virtual call.
body_markdown:
*Some of your most important sales conversations never touch Zoom. Now you can record them, score them, and coach on them like any other call.*


It's 2:15 on a Thursday. Your field rep is sitting in a customer's back office, holding a cup of coffee that has clearly been on the burner since the morning shift.


Forty minutes in, the buyer leans back and says the thing. The real reason they left their last vendor. The name of the person who actually signs. The objection they've been too polite to raise on any call.


It's the most valuable minute of the quarter. Your rep nods thoughtfully. They don't write it down, because scribbling mid-sentence while someone is opening up is a great way to make them stop.


Then comes the parking lot. Another meeting. A drive-thru. A call from their manager about a different deal.


Three hours later, the CRM entry reads:


> *Great meeting. Very interested. Follow up next week.*


That's it. The most important conversation of the quarter, compressed into eight words and a vibe.


If that meeting had happened on Zoom, you'd have the recording, a score, and the exact moment the objection came up. Because it happened across a table, you have a sticky note's worth of memory.


In-Person Recording fixes that.


‍


‍


## **The two-tier coaching problem nobody planned for**


Here's how most sales teams quietly end up working.


Comparison


The rep on Zoom The rep in the field


What they get Game film Folklore


How the conversation is captured Recorded, scored, and broken down automatically A CRM note and whatever they remember on the drive back


What the manager coaches from The exact second a discovery question landed or a pricing objection went sideways A hallway debrief


How accurate it is Exactly what was said Usually generous to the rep


Nobody designed it this way. It just happened, because the tools were built around the calendar invite with a video link in it. The conversations that happen across a table, at a booth, or over lunch slipped through the gap.


And those are rarely the throwaway conversations. They're the site visits, the meetings with the executive who doesn't do video, and the relationship moments that move deals.


### **Even teams that record have a gap**


Some teams already solved the capture part. Reps carry a separate recorder, or they use another conversation intelligence tool for field meetings.


That's better than nothing. But now the field recordings live in one place and your coaching lives in another. The scoring, review, and coaching your managers do on virtual calls never touches those conversations.


So you end up with a complete picture of how your team sells on video, and a partial one of how they sell in person.


You can't coach what you can't see. You definitely can't coach what's sitting in a different app.


‍


## **Hit record. Have the conversation. That's the whole training.**


Quick context if you're new here: Hyperbound is an AI sales coaching platform. Teams use it to practice with realistic AI roleplays, and to score and analyze their real sales calls so reps and managers can see what's working. That second part is called Hyperbound Perform.


In-Person Recording is a new recorder inside Perform. It runs in the browser, so there's nothing to download and no app store involved.


Here's what a rep actually does:


1. Open app.hyperbound.ai/real-calls/record in a phone or laptop browser, or start it from Real Calls, the page where the team's recorded calls live.
2. With the buyer's OK, tap record and set the phone on the table. There's a pause button if someone needs to step out. No bot joining, no calendar invite, no app to install.
3. When it's over, tap stop. Give the meeting a title and add who else was there. It's optional, but names are how the transcript labels who said what.
4. Link the deal it belongs to, then tap Save meeting. The meeting shows up on that deal's timeline.


That's it. Usually within about a minute, the meeting is transcribed, scored against your team's scorecards (the criteria that define a good call, like asking strong discovery questions), and sitting in Real Calls next to every video call. Hyperbound flags Moments: the key points worth a second look, like how an objection was handled.


Several people talking into one phone? Because the rep adds who was in the room, the transcript labels who said what. The review doesn't read like one long monologue.


And field meetings have a habit of happening in basements, warehouses, and buildings where cell service goes to die. The recorder saves audio on the device in short clips and uploads as it goes, so a bad signal shouldn't cost you the meeting.


It won't whisper advice in your rep's ear mid-meeting. It just makes sure the meeting still exists after everyone leaves the room.


And it's included in Perform. No add-on, no separate pricing, no procurement email.


‍


## **Five places your best conversations are hiding**


### **1. The across-the-table meeting**


**Who:** A field rep visiting a prospect at their place of business.


No screen share, no meeting link, just two people and a table. The rep opens Hyperbound on their phone, starts recording in Real Calls, and gets on with the meeting. Afterward they save it, add who was there, and confirm the deal. Hyperbound scores it like any other call.


**What changes:** The follow-up email quotes what the buyer actually said, not what the rep thinks they said. On Monday, the manager coaches on the real meeting instead of the reenactment.


### **2. The team that already records, just somewhere else**


**Who:** A sales manager whose field team records meetings with a separate recorder or another tool.


The habit is already there. The problem is the destination. Those recordings never reach the platform where the manager reviews performance and builds coaching.


**What changes:** Reps keep recording, they just do it in Hyperbound. In-person meetings land next to virtual calls in the same scoring and review. For the rep, the only change is which button they press. For the manager, it's the first complete view of how the whole team sells.


### **3. The conference booth**


**Who:** A rep working a trade show, having fifteen good conversations before lunch.


By 4pm, every booth conversation blurs together. Which one was the VP with the budget problem? Which one asked about the integration?


**What changes:** Record the conversations that matter (with permission), submit them between sessions, and let Hyperbound flag the key moments. Post-event follow-up starts from what each person actually said, not from a stack of badge scans.


### **4. The coffee meeting**


**Who:** An account executive who does some of their best selling over coffee or lunch.


These are the conversations with no agenda and no calendar invite. They're also where relationships move.


**What changes:** Recording takes a few taps in a phone browser, so the unplanned conversation gets the same treatment as the scheduled one.


### **5. The new field hire**


**Who:** A manager ramping a new field rep who can't ride along to every meeting.


Ramp is when coaching matters most, and when a manager's calendar makes it hardest. Shadowing every first meeting isn't realistic.


**What changes:** The new rep records their early meetings, and the manager reviews the scored conversation and the key moments. Feedback is based on what happened in the room, not a hallway debrief.


‍


## **The part that actually changes**


Recording a conversation in person isn't new. Plenty of tools can capture audio in a room.


What changes is where that conversation goes next.


- **One standard for every conversation.** Field meetings get scored against the same scorecards as virtual calls. A great discovery is a great discovery, whether it happened on video or over a conference table.
- **Coaching from the source, not the summary.** Managers review what was said, not a rep's recollection three hours and one drive-thru later.
- **Field reps finally get game film.** The reps doing the hardest, most relationship-heavy selling get the same quality of feedback as their inside teammates.
- **The meeting stays with the deal.** In-person conversations land on the deal's timeline, so whoever picks up the deal can hear what was actually said.
- **One place, not two.** Teams already recording in person can stop splitting conversations across tools.
- **No rollout project.** No bot, no calendar invite, no app to install. If your reps can open a browser and tap a button, they're onboarded.


The CRM note doesn't go away. It just stops being the only record of the most important meeting of the week.


‍
